newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court to hear death-row inmate's appeal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court to hear death-row inmate's appeal.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court said on Thursday it would hear an appeal by Virginia death-row inmate Joseph O'Dell, whose case has been championed by capital punishment opponents and by Pope John Paul II.

The high court, in a brief order, announced it would hear arguments in the case next year, with a ruling due by the end of its 1996-97 term in June. The justices on Tuesday granted O'Dell a last-minute stay of execution while it considers his case.

The Supreme Court said it would consider O'Dell's arguments that the jury in his case should have been told he could have been sentenced to life in prison without parole as an alternative to a death sentence.

The justices will decide whether their 1994 decision requiring that a jury be told of the possible life-in-prison sentence applies retroactively to cases in which the sentence already had been handed down.
The Supreme Court, however, refused to consider O'Dell's other argument claiming new DNA evidence casts doubt on his murder conviction.

O'Dell, convicted in 1986 of raping and murdering a 44-year-old secretary, had been scheduled to die by lethal injection on Wednesday night. His case has sparked a plea for clemency from the Vatican and street protests in Rome, where it has been widely publicised.
